newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Troops wound four Arabs near Bethlehem holy site.
newsitem.headline: Troops wound four Arabs near Bethlehem holy site.

text.p: Israeli troops wounded four Arabs, among them a Palestinian police colonel, during a fiery protest on Wednesday at a Jewish holy site near the PLO-ruled West Bank town of Bethlehem, witnesses said.
The Israeli army said Palestinian protesters fired on the troops, and that two soldiers were lightly injured by petrol bombs and stones thrown at them.

The incident followed clashes in Ramallah, north of Bethlehem, in which soldiers shot dead four Palestinians and wounded up to 300 in the bloodiest West Bank fighting since Palestinian self-rule began there two years ago.

Witnesses said Palestinian demonstrators built a large bonfire next to Rachel's Tomb, threw volleys of petrol bombs, and threatened to destroy the structure, by tradition the grave of the wife of the biblical patriarch Jacob.
Israeli troops, recoiling from a storm of hurled stones, then opened fire with rubber bullets and live ammunition, the witnesses said.

They said Colonel Kifah Barakat, local commander of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's Force 17, was struck in the face by a rubber bullet while trying to mediate an end to the Bethlehem street battles.

The clashes on Wednesday were part of widespread protests in the West Bank and Gaza Strip against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to open a tunnel in Jerusalem near Islam's third holiest shrine.

The tomb of Rachel has been a focus of political strife in recent months. Israelis have stirred Palestinian ire by barricading off a lane of the main Bethlehem-Jerusalem road near the tomb to facilitate construction work developing the site.
